text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unions hold out on airline rescue: CAW, CUPE won't take pay cut unless governments chip in $400-million for Canadian.
- Health Minister David Dingwall takes aim at child poverty.
- Erasing measles possible by 2000: Canadian cases drop with program.
- Spring vote possible to deal with Parti Quebecois rift.
- Health-care coffers refilled by Klein: Election not a factor, Tories say.
- Prime Minister's brief visit reveals strong China ties: Li goes out of his way to be with Jean Chretien during six-hour stop.
- Markets keep steaming ahead: TSE's booming bank stocks overcome gold weakness; Dow jumps 76 points to record.
- Biovail news aids shares: Litigation settled, new drugs planned.
- Manulife takeover offer for Altamira called illegal: Insurer dismisses concern raised by Almiria shareholders.

- Canadian talks at standstill: Two of the airline's big unions tell Transport Minister David Anderson they won't accept wage cuts. Anderson tells them Ottawa won't help keep Canadian in the skies unless they make a deal.
- End of Biovail dispute may open US$700-million market.
